item.title: Jakoten: Uwajima's Fried Fish Cake — Guide
item.description: Jakoten is one of the great local foods of southern Ehime, especially the Uwajima and Yawatahama area, where the rich fishing grounds of the Uwa Sea supply the small fish it’s made from. Unlike refined white fish paste, jakoten is made by grinding up whole small fish — bones, skin and all — then deep-frying the mixture into a flat, golden-brown cake with a robust, savoury flavour and a slightly coarse texture full of the taste of the sea.

item.title: Uwajima Toro Nagashi Lantern Floating — Guide
item.description: Toro nagashi is a gentle, deeply moving Japanese tradition held during the Obon season in summer, when the spirits of ancestors are believed to return and then depart again. In Uwajima on Ehime’s southern coast, glowing paper lanterns — each carrying a candle and often a prayer or the name of a departed loved one — are set adrift on the water at dusk, floating out across the bay in a slow, shimmering procession of light to guide the souls of the dead peacefully back to the other world.

item.title: Uwajima Ushioni Festival — Guide
item.description: The Uwajima Ushioni Festival is the great summer celebration of the southern city of Uwajima, held in late July. Its unmistakable symbol is the ushioni or ‘sea ox’, a fantastical monster float several metres long with a body draped in red cloth or palm fibre, a long neck, and a fierce demon-like head, carried by teams of young people who make it lunge, sway and ‘battle’ through the streets to drive away evil spirits and pray for good health.

item.title: Ehime Events & Festivals: Niihama Taiko, Matsuyama Autumn & Uwajima Ushi-oni
item.description: Ehime’s festival calendar is anchored at one end by one of the largest and most physically intense portable shrine festivals in all of Japan, and at the other by a winter onsen illumination that turns the country’s oldest hot spring building into something from a fever dream. Between those poles, bull-demons rampage through Uwajima, Matsuyama fills with dancers, and the Seto Inland Sea reflects summer fireworks from the bridges of Shimanami Kaido.
